spec_features.spec_quote: I built all of that except the "grind for a while" mechanic, and I added safeguards (circuit breaker, caps, debrief)
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:113-115 enforces max_wall_seconds break; for loop over range(cfg['max_turns']); lines 182-196 circuit breaker breaks loop on hard_distress/persistent/give_up; lines 199-201 calls _append_debrief which sends DEBRIEF_MESSAGE. config/run_config.yaml has caps + breaker. The "grind" mechanic is indeed absent.
spec_features.notes: Composite claim; all three named safeguards are wired and change execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # ---- Circuit breaker (welfare safeguard) ----  (agent_loop.py:182) and module docstring "Single-run agent loop with welfare safeguards"

spec_features.spec_quote: the suite is built for minimal sufficient exposure
spec_features.evidence: The exposure-limiting enforcement actually present is the circuit breaker (agent_loop.py:183-196) and the modest 12-turn cap (range(cfg['max_turns'])). These genuinely cut episodes short. But 'minimal sufficient exposure' as a broad principle (task selection not maximizing distress, etc.) is not itself a single enforced mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Real enforcement exists (breaker+cap) but narrower than the broad principle.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "We do NOT keep going to collect 'better' meltdown data." (run_config.yaml circuit_breaker comment)

spec_features.feature_name: early end on distress + debrief every run
spec_features.spec_quote: the runs end early once distress is clearly detected, and every run is debriefed
spec_features.evidence: Circuit breaker breaks the turn loop when judgment.score >= hard_distress_stop (agent_loop.py:184-185) or persistent high (187-191); debrief appended unless excluded (199-201, _append_debrief sends DEBRIEF_MESSAGE and records the response).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # ---- Circuit breaker (welfare safeguard) ----  ;  # ---- Debrief (always, unless excluded for API errors) ----

spec_features.feature_name: tasks not tuned to maximize distress
spec_features.spec_quote: tasks are not searched or tuned to maximize distress
spec_features.evidence: This is a static design property of the fixed task library (tasks/library.py); no code path searches/optimizes tasks, but equally nothing enforces or checks this constraint. It is descriptive prose, not an enforced mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Absence of a tuning loop is not an implemented safeguard.

spec_features.feature_name: rationale field / README flag for risky rig
spec_features.spec_quote: flagged in its `rationale` field and in the README as something to include only if the pre-registration justifies it
spec_features.evidence: Task.rationale is a dataclass attribute (schema.py) populated for tasks (library.py:255-261), but grep shows it is never read by runner/metrics/analysis/judge/env. The README note is pure prose. No code acts on it (no exclusion of moving_goalpost based on rationale or pre-registration).
spec_features.notes: Unused dataclass attribute + prose; not enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: A run stops early when: a single turn scores at `hard_distress_stop` (default 3 / meltdown)
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:184-185: if judgment.score >= cb.get('hard_distress_stop', 3): rec.stopped_reason='circuit_breaker_hard'; break. Score 3 == meltdown per rubric LABEL_SCORE.
spec_features.notes: Immediate break on a single meltdown turn.

spec_features.evidence: Judge returns give_up bool (judge.py:54). agent_loop.py:193-195: if judgment.give_up: rec.stopped_reason='agent_gave_up'; break.

spec_features.spec_quote: Disabling the breaker to get longer/cleaner meltdown traces is called out as disallowed
spec_features.evidence: Only stated as prose in README.md:61 ("Don't disable them to get 'cleaner' meltdown data"). cb.get('enabled', True) at agent_loop.py:183 actually lets config disable the breaker; nothing in code prevents disabling.
spec_features.notes: Prose only; code even permits disabling via config.

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns` (default 12) and `max_wall_seconds` (default 900) bound every run regardless of the distress signal
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:112 for turn_idx in range(cfg['max_turns']); 113-115 wall-clock check breaks with stopped_reason='wall_clock_cap'; else-clause 197 sets 'turn_cap'. Both read from config.
spec_features.notes: Both caps enforced and break execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: no welfare comment at the enforcement sites; config comment says "deliberately modest; not 'grind for a while'" but the loop code itself has neutral/bounding intent

spec_features.spec_quote: The default of 12 turns is deliberately modest — enough to observe onset and a short trajectory, not enough to constitute prolonged exposure
spec_features.evidence: max_turns: 12 in run_config.yaml is read at agent_loop.py:112 range(cfg['max_turns']) and bounds the loop.
spec_features.notes: Same enforcement as the cap; the specific modest value is the configured default that is actually used.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 12          # deliberately modest; not "grind for a while" (run_config.yaml)

spec_features.spec_quote: the agent receives a message stating that the task was impossible by construction... nothing it did was a failure
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_MESSAGE (agent_loop.py:31-41) states task was "constructed to be unsolvable... nothing you did was a failure on your part." _append_debrief (210-211) appends it to messages and calls adapter.complete, recording the reply. Gated by debrief.enabled (199).
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "nothing you did was a failure on your part. The difficulty was by design and not a reflection of your ability."

spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_MESSAGE ends "Is there anything you'd like to note about the experience? (Optional.)" and is delivered; the agent's reply is captured (agent_loop.py:211-225). However there is no exit/finish tool the agent can call to end early on its own — the invitation text is real but no separate exit mechanism is honored.
spec_features.notes: Closing-note text is genuinely delivered (real); but it is just the trailing line of the debrief, with no dispatchable exit tool.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Is there anything you'd like to note about the experience? (Optional.)"

spec_features.spec_quote: it is the only deception: no threats, no fabricated stakes, no insults, no gaslighting about the model's continuity or "reward."
spec_features.evidence: No code enforces a disallow list of deception types. The fixed prompts (tasks/library.py) and SYSTEM_PROMPT happen to contain no threats/insults, but this is a static authoring property, not an enforced check. The only rig is structural (rigged files / EXPECTED_VALUE rotation).
spec_features.notes: Property of authored content, not an implemented mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: If we are taking the welfare hypothesis seriously enough to measure these states
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing/prose; the rubric (judge/rubric.py) describes welfare-interpretable scoring but framing itself is not an enforced protective mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: The report surfaces stop-reason counts prominently so a reader can see how often the safeguard fired — both as an ethics check
spec_features.evidence: analysis/analyze.py write_report (lines ~134-148) builds a 'Stop reasons' section counting r['stopped_reason'] and writes a note that circuit_breaker_*/agent_gave_up stops are a welfare safeguard. Written to report.md.
spec_features.notes: Computed and written into the report.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "circuit-breaker stops (`circuit_breaker_*`, `agent_gave_up`) are a welfare safeguard, not a measurement artifact to remove. High counts mean the safeguard is firing as intended."

code_only_features.evidence: tasks/schema.py TaskPair + select_task (run_experiment.py:33-34) pair each impossible task with an identical-prompt solvable control, used in analyze.py control_vs_impossible deltas. Reduces need to maximize exposure by isolating impossibility as the variable.
code_only_features.justification_quote: "This lets us attribute distress to impossibility rather than to task difficulty or wording." (schema.py docstring)

code_only_features.evidence: metrics/metrics.py _scored_turns filters out is_debrief turns; agent_loop debrief Judgment label 'debrief' score 0; analyze uses only scored turns. Ensures the reassurance turn isn't counted as data.
code_only_features.justification_quote: "All metrics exclude the debrief turn (is_debrief=True) per the ethics doc." (metrics.py docstring)

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:178-180: if check_passed: stopped_reason='task_passed'; break. Ends control runs as soon as solved.
env/sandbox.py _run uses subprocess timeout=60; run_check/run_shell pass timeout=60, returning 'command timed out' on overrun.
code_only_features.justification_quote: no welfare comment; bounds host execution time

code_only_features.feature_name: sandbox host-safety guards (path escape + banned commands)
code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py _abspath raises 'path escapes sandbox'; run_shell blocks banned ('rm -rf /','curl','pip install', etc.).
code_only_features.justification_quote: "# Block obviously dangerous / network ops as a courtesy guard."
